_comment: Rules and anti-rules published after a release, so an installed Fox-Grade keeps improving without waiting for
one. Fetched at most once every twenty hours, cached, and merged on top of the tables that ship in the jar.
It can only add. The bundled tables load first and are never replaced, so a feed that is empty, stale,
unreachable or malformed leaves Fox-Grade exactly as it was built. It carries data, not code: blocklist entries
and bridge-table rows, parsed into the same structures the bundled files parse into.
Turn it off with "rulesFeed": false in fox-grade.config.json, which stops the request rather than ignoring
mixinBlocklist takes the same shape as the bundled mixin-blocklist.json: entries of {mixin, methods}, where an
absent or empty methods list means the whole mixin is disabled. apiBridges takes the same shape as
Every entry here should say why it exists. A rule nobody can check is one nobody can remove.
